correctness.rationale: Definition 4.2 adds the same increment to every positive grade of a factor, so their offsets from the top grade are exact invariants. If s_m is the separate top-grade effect and c=(H(d)-sum s_m)/n, then e_m=s_m-x_top,m. Efficiency fixes the sum of top grades, and the top-grade error relative to s_m+c is multiplied by 1-n alpha. This proves the claimed full limit and its iff compatibility criterion for 0<alpha<2/n. Subtracting the PCOMR equations at k and at d_m fixes the offset at H(d_-m,k)-H(d), not the EAIE offset. In the (2,1) witness the only nonzero grid value is H(1,1)=1. The payoff (1,0,0) satisfies all PCOMR equations and top efficiency. All separate effects and the balance term vanish; both top excesses vanish, so the correction and stopping discrepancy are identically zero at this non-EAIE point. Two factors and one lower positive grade are minimal within the stated scope. This is an exact hand reconstruction against the source definitions, not execution of the bundled verify.py or a formal certificate.
